metadata.case_name: LO CHUEN CHUNG v. WONG CHUN SING

injuries.description: the plaintiff suffered multiple injuries to the face, nose and right eye, including rupture of the right eyeball and extrusion of the crystalline lens.
source: the plaintiff suffered multiple injuries to the face, nose and right eye, including rupture of the right eyeball and extrusion of the crystalline lens.
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration or rupture with prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

injuries.description: post-traumatic aphakia and aniridia involving scleral fixation of an intra-ocular lens with artificial iris.
source: he underwent three operations between the date of the accident and 1 March 2004 when he the final operation was performed for post-traumatic aphakia and aniridia involving scleral fixation of an intra-ocular lens with artificial iris.

injuries.description: the plaintiff had suffered from glaucoma but this had been successfully treated with eye drops.
source: the plaintiff had suffered from glaucoma but this had been successfully treated with eye drops.

manifestations.description: the plaintiff's vision in his right eye was poor. The best-corrected distant visual acuity was 0.3 for the right eye as against the 1.0 for the left eye. For both eyes together, it was 1.0.
the best-corrected visual acuity of 20/50 for the right eye as against 20/20 for the left eye (Dr Cheung's finding).
unable to tolerate optical correction due to anisometropia (the discrepancy between the optical corrections).
loss of stereopsis for the judgment of distance and depth.
photophobia in the right eye; may have to wear sunglasses and eye may become tired if he had to drive for long hours under the sun.
permanent impairment of visual function, according to the AMA guide, of 29% (Dr Chua).
impairment of the whole visual system at 17% (Dr Cheung).

treatments_received: three operations between the date of the accident and 1 March 2004
scleral fixation of an intra-ocular lens with artificial iris (operation performed 1 March 2004)
treatments_future: follow-up treatment for 12 months at a cost of $5,000 (private sector estimate by Dr Chua)
possible future operation for further retinal detachment (cost estimate $60,000 by Dr Chua)
possible operation for post-traumatic glaucoma (cost estimate $40,000 by Dr Chua)
Dr Cheung: follow-up for glaucoma for about 7 years involving about 15 check-ups at $40 each in the public sector or $1,000 each in the private sector

losses.description: Permanent impairment of visual function and loss of visual capacity in the right eye (rupture of right eyeball, extrusion of crystalline lens, aphakia, aniridia).
Unable to return to pre-accident employment as a driver because of loss of ability to judge distance and depth; can only work as an office assistant.
